title: Google Analytics Pricing: Free vs 360 Costs in 2026
summary: Google Analytics pricing includes a free plan with caps on data exports and retention, and Analytics 360 as a custom-priced paid option.
body_markdown:
## Frequently asked questions


### Is Google Analytics really free?


Yes, for most businesses the standard version of Google Analytics costs nothing to use.


What you pay for is what sits around it: the limits on how much data you can export and how much gets sampled in reports, and the paid tools you add when you hit those limits.


If your reporting stays inside the ceilings, the bill stays at zero.


Do you need Analytics 360 for more than one website? No. The free version can collect data from several websites and apps, and you can combine them in one property or keep them in separate ones.


Analytics 360 is the paid tier you move to when limits on volume, export or sampling start to block your reporting. Having a second site isn't the trigger.


### Does Google use my Google Analytics data?


Google processes the data to run the product, and that's the trade-off behind a free tool. Several settings control whether it is also shared for other purposes, such as benchmarking or product improvement, and whether it feeds advertising features.


You should open the data-sharing settings in your account and switch off what you don't want. Review them after any setup change, because they are easy to leave at their defaults.


If you operate under privacy rules such as GDPR, a lawyer or privacy officer should check your configuration, not this article.


### Can I export my Google Analytics data if I switch?


Partly, and this is where the real cost of leaving shows up. You can pull reports and raw event data out, but the interface and API cap what you get, and large exports may be sampled or limited.


Start exporting to a warehouse before you decide to leave; that's the cleanest route. A warehouse copy is the history you control. If you wait until the day you switch, you take whatever the limits allow, and that may not be everything you need.


### Is Universal Analytics still available?


No. Universal Analytics, the previous generation, has been replaced by Google Analytics 4, and new data no longer flows into it.


Historical reports from the old system were only available for a limited period, so anything you didn't export is likely gone or going.


If you still need that history for year-on-year comparison, find out what you saved before you build any plans that depend on it.
